message.text: Role execution complies with strict boundaries: D11-R1 (Sandbox Build) and D11-R2 (Real-World Stress Probe) executed strictly by assigned specialist eric; reviewer audit gate executed by reviewer with zero orchestrator inline bypass.

All required deliverables exist on disk and SHA-256 checksums match output/SHA256SUMS.txt cryptographically with zero discrepancies (index_metrics.json, indexing_benchmark_summary.md, partial_index_write_amplification_report.md, write_amplification_metrics.json).

Hero metric confirmed: Exactly 1,000,000 synthetic rows verified in table d11_indexing_sandbox.orders with 95/5 skew (49,888 active rows [4.99%], 700,058 completed rows [70.01%], 250,054 archived rows [25.01%]) on PostgreSQL 18.0 port 5433.

Hero metric confirmed: Query latency slashed from 163.43 ms sequential scan baseline down to 0.096 ms on partial index scan (1,702.4x server speedup; 99.87% shared buffer block reduction from 77,144 blocks to 104 blocks).

Hero metric confirmed: Partial index disk footprint is 1.09 MB (1,138,688 bytes) compared to 38.32 MB (40,181,760 bytes) for full composite index, delivering 97.17% physical disk savings (surpassing the >=75% SLA threshold).

Hero metric confirmed: Inactive row write maintenance eliminated 100% (645 pages written vs 0 pages written), eliminating 95% of total index maintenance overhead under 95/5 skew; overall write throughput increased by +75.45% (53,837.2 to 94,457.8 TPS) across 100,000 rapid operations.

Planner probe confirmed: Cost-based query planner selects partial index idx_orders_partial_active_created over sequential scan for complex filter WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' AND created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '1 day', yielding 90.3x speedup and 98.6% buffer I/O reduction (ordered limit query execution: 0.124 ms).

Expression index probe confirmed: JSONB partial expression index idx_orders_partial_urgent_jsonb isolates 12,516 urgent rows (1.25%) into a 296.00 KB footprint, delivering sub-millisecond document query execution (0.062 ms vs 235.6 ms seq scan; 3,800.7x speedup).
Strict zero em dashes check passed: 0 em dashes detected across all SQL scripts, Python harnesses, markdown reports, JSON manifests, and documentation.
